failures.reader_effect: The reader cannot reliably picture who occupies which entrance/exit, what physically or socially prevents movement, or why previously declared blockers/observers cease to matter. This produces 'how can one door hold all those people?' and rear-alley continuity disbelief rather than useful uncertainty.
failures.hard_rule: Any scene that introduces a blocked exit, crowd, pursuer, watcher, guard line, or physical barrier must resolve or causally transform that constraint before characters use the route. Do not rely on invisible off-page disappearance. A barrier only holds a group if a material, legal, social, tactical, or motivational reason is legible in the scene.

failures.reader_effect: After the opening escape, the story proceeds through too many full-stop travel/checkpoint scenes, each individually functional but cumulatively slow. The reader experiences repeated move -> stop -> explain/discover -> move cycles and loses desire to continue.
failures.hard_rule: Adjacent scenes must not be preserved merely because each has a distinct local function. If multiple consecutive scenes mainly move route, reveal a clue, re-state trust, or process injury, merge/cut/reorder until the forward objective changes faster. Scene uniqueness is not pacing proof.
